note: Enntity/atlas inkling2/concurrent-spec-20261123: the Inkling 2 Mini (model type inkling2_loop) serving series, 59 commits on Atlas-Inf main 269b533bc (Merge #332). It parses the checkpoint as 48 unrolled layer visits, checks its layout at load, and adds the inkling-2-mini kernel target: decode attention with relative bias and per-token sinks, short convolutions with verify rollback, block attention residuals, loop message gates, NVFP4 and MXFP8 stacked-expert MoE decode, prefill experts at the checkpoint's declared numerics (W4A4 / W8A8 on the block-scaled tensor cores), GQA flash prefill attention, CUDA-graph single- and multi-sequence decode (BF16 projections of up to 8 rows on the batched GEMV, each row computed as the one-row GEMV computes it; with the checkpoint's weights a visit's input projections run as one launch), the Spark NVFP4 overlay for decode and verify (attention projections, the experts of layers 20-23, lm_head; prefill reads the checkpoint's own tensors in both modes), programmatic dependent launch for the target's kernels (always on), and the checkpoint's DSpark drafter on the DFlash head. The scheduler tracks the reasoning block and closes it with <|end_message|> once it runs past its effort's budget or loops (budget forcing). Tool-call arguments stream as they are generated, and the tool guard's stream setting checks each call when it ends instead of holding it. Prefix caching carries each visit's short-conv state on the cache's snapshots, a prompt under 512 tokens skips the tail-checkpoint split, an exact replay of a block-aligned prompt restores its tail checkpoint, a prompt that forks from a cached one can save a checkpoint at the fork (branch checkpoints, now for aux-state models too), and the disk tier restores evicted KV only up to a snapshot; the checkpoint's vision tower (a 23-layer ViT with axial RoPE and layer scale on the shared ViT kernels, one image token per 40x40 pixel tile, no resize), with token embeddings normed once at load so image rows skip the embedding norm as in the reference. A call written with no block header (a forced tool choice) is read as the answer. With two live requests the DSpark proposes share one vocabulary-head pass, an operator depth table bounds their drafts, and a pair whose drafts stop paying decodes plain until a re-probe. The drafter reports each draft's confidence, so a verify can stop where it is unsure, and the rule that turns drafts off for a sequence weighs each step by the drafts it verified and waits a short time before its first re-probe. Proposed upstream to Atlas-Inf.
